system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “standard market” characterisation is advocacy, not an agreed position. Against the AUD 24 million debt-free/cash-free deal, I recommend the following buyer positions:

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m). | A higher cap, preferably the full price for general warranties, with separate treatment for specific indemnities and uncapped fraud. | **Reject 20%; seek a materially higher cap.** AUD 4.8m may not cover aggregated losses from undisclosed liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 tipping/excess-only basket. | Lower de minimis and a tipping basket, or a lower deductible basket; clarify aggregation and related claims. | **Counter with a lower de minimis and tipping basket.** The proposed deductible structure leaves the Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 as well as sub-threshold claims. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months; Seller says limits apply to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period for general warranties and express, tailored periods for tax, fundamental/title and indemnity claims. | **Seek at least 24 months for general claims and express carve-outs.** Eighteen months may be too short to discover and quantify latent issues. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits. | Fundamental and title claims outside the general cap, with a substantially higher (ideally price-level) cap and longer limitation period. | **Reject the general regime for these claims.** A 20% cap is inconsistent with the core bargain of acquiring 100% of the shares. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all claims; no express fraud carve-out stated. | Express carve-outs for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation (including as to cap, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance), subject to applicable law. | **Require an express carve-out.** The Buyer should not contractually limit remedies for fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records; specific disclosures also given. | Specific, fair disclosure against the relevant warranty, with sufficient detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room/public-register disclosure. | **Reject blanket general disclosure.** It risks turning an indexed room or public record into a broad, uncertain warranty exception. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | At most, limit the qualifier to actual knowledge of named individuals, without imputed or constructive knowledge; preserve claims for fraud and specific indemnities. | **Reject the proposed wording.** “Discoverable” knowledge is broad and could make diligence itself a defence to a warranty claim. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller to use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DD-002 shows ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%), change-of-control conditions and no final consent or evidence conditions are met. | Completion condition requiring final, unconditional written consent and satisfaction/waiver of all applicable conditions, with no adverse variation; Buyer termination right if unmet. | **Make this a genuine condition precedent, not deemed satisfied on consent alone.** Bluefen is a major revenue source and the contractual conditions also need addressing. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | ~AUD 3.2m facility to be released after Completion. DD-003 says it remains outstanding and no final discharge is included. | Repayment at or before Completion from Seller’s proceeds (or agreed price adjustment), plus lender payoff evidence and effective release of all security as a completion deliverable. | **Do not accept post-Completion release.** The debt-free/cash-free basis requires the debt and security to be cleared as part of Completion. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are omitted from funds flow and are “for the Seller”; on-cost treatment unspecified. | Identify and quantify bonuses and payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs; allocate them to Seller, with payment/withholding and evidence handled at Completion or a specific adjustment/indemnity. | **Require explicit funds-flow treatment and Seller responsibility.** The omitted amount and potentially additional on-costs could otherwise reduce the acquired company’s value. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-004 says transfer depends on all SOW3 fees being cleared; DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open but is not independent verification, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the room. | Require verified payment of all SOW3 fees and a valid written assignment/confirmation of all relevant IP before Completion; retain a specific indemnity covering title, ownership, non-infringement and resulting losses if not resolved. | **Do not accept a payment-only indemnity.** Payment alone does not establish that the Company has received the necessary IP rights. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | DD-006 called preliminary and not expected to be material; Seller proposes no special treatment. Disclosure says an unintended external link may have exposed ~1,240 records, with access, scope and notification status unresolved. | Full investigation and disclosure before signing/Completion; appropriate remediation and any legally required notifications; specific indemnity for the incident and resulting claims, costs and regulatory action, without relying on general caps/baskets. | **Treat as a live, unresolved risk, not immaterial by assumption.** The exposure and response obligations remain unverified. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 described as ordinary-course operating costs. DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together; termination, accrual and avoidability are not stated. | Confirm timing, terms, commitments, termination rights, accrued amounts and whether costs are reflected in working capital; include appropriate adjustment or specific protection for undisclosed/unprovided commitments. | **Seek the underlying contracts and a clear economic allocation.** “Ordinary course” does not establish whether the commitments are avoidable or already reflected in price. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all claims; tax and IP treated under the general regime. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, fraud and any agreed special risks; state each category’s cap, time limit and interaction with remedies. | **Reject an all-claims blanket regime.** Different claim types and risks require express, workable treatment rather than defaulting all to general limits. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register recording Seller as holder of 100%; no separate verification indicated. | Verify constitution, register, share certificates and ASIC/company records; confirm shares are fully paid and free of encumbrances, with title warranties and completion transfer documents. | **Do not treat the register alone as conclusive verification.** It is an important source, but the Buyer should check the transfer chain and completion mechanics. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP positions are settled under the general regime, but no detailed terms are supplied. | Negotiate express tax and IP warranties and, where appropriate, separate specific indemnities, caps and survival periods; confirm treatment of pre-Completion tax and IP ownership/assignment risks. | **Keep these terms open pending drafting and diligence.** The Seller’s summary does not specify protections adequate to assess or accept. |

These are negotiation recommendations based on the supplied summary and disclosure letter, not a review of the complete SPA or underlying data-room documents. The Buyer’s lawyers should confirm the final drafting and any statutory notification or remediation obligations.
=== END ADVICE ===
